verdict: Cardinal Health revenue rose 5% to $67.5B and GAAP profit rose 23% to $554M, powered by its giant pharmaceutical distribution business — and management raised the full-year outlook.

segments.name: Pharmaceutical & Specialty Solutions
segments.note: Distributing brand and specialty medicines to hospitals and pharmacies — segment profit rose 17% to $783M. Shown $23M below the reported $62,582M so the segments add exactly to total revenue (see footer).

segments.name: Global Medical Products & Distribution
segments.note: Medical and lab products and distribution — revenue flat at $3.2B, and segment profit fell 28% to $33M on distribution and currency headwinds.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Nuclear and precision health, at-home supplies and OptiFreight logistics — segment profit rose 16% to $193M, the highest-margin piece at about 11%.

opex.name: Distribution, selling, general & admin, net
opex.note: Warehouses, delivery and running the company ($1,595M), net of a $47M litigation recovery and a $4M gain on asset disposals credited in operating expenses.

opex.name: Amortization & acquisition costs
opex.note: Amortization and other costs tied to acquisitions — up from $104M a year ago.

opex.name: Acquisition-related compensation
opex.note: Cash and share-based pay tied to physician-practice acquisitions.

takeaways.title: Pharma distribution is carrying the growth
takeaways.text: Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions profit rose 17% to $783M on brand and specialty drug growth and a strong generics program — it earns more than the rest of the company combined many times over.

takeaways.title: Medical products is the weak spot
takeaways.text: Global Medical Products and Distribution profit fell 28% to just $33M on flat $3.2B revenue, hit by distribution and currency effects, partly offset by its own-brand products.

takeaways.title: Full-year guidance raised
takeaways.text: Management lifted fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $12.80–$13.00 and completed a $500M share buyback in the quarter. GAAP EPS of $2.38 sits below non-GAAP $3.26 mainly because of $182M of amortization and acquisition costs.

oneTimers: A $47M litigation recovery (a benefit) inside operating expenses this quarter, vs no such item a year ago.

Non-GAAP results exclude $182M of amortization and other acquisition-related costs, $94M of acquisition-related compensation and $23M of restructuring — the gap between GAAP EPS of $2.38 and non-GAAP EPS of $3.26.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $73M, partly offset by $6M of other income and a $2M gain on completing the sale of the Outcomes stake — a net $65M cost.
footerNote: The three reported segment revenues ($62,582M + $3,190M + $1,764M) sum to $67,536M, $23M above the $67,513M total — the release notes segment sums reflect rounding. The largest segment is shown $23M lower so the pieces add exactly. The flow uses total net earnings of $556M; after $2M attributable to noncontrolling interests, net earnings attributable to Cardinal Health were $554M ($2.38 per diluted share). Cardinal Health's fiscal year ends June 30, so this is Q1 of fiscal 2027.
